 Relentless storms keep Florida coast on high alert as catastrophic flooding continues
 NOAA's Weather Prediction Center (WPC) has issued a Level 4 out of 4 High flash flood risk for the coast from the Daytona Beach area southward to Rockledge Friday.
 By
 Alexandra Myers , Julian Atienza 
 Source
 FOX Weather
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 Email 
 Copy Link
 06:44 Rare level 4 of 4 coastal flood threat continue across Florida's Atlantic Coast 
 Cities along Florida's Atlantic Coast are facing an elevated flash flood threat again on Friday. Up to two feet of rain is possible throughout the region. FOX Weather Correspondent Brandy Campbell reports in Cocoa, Florida, amid ankle-deep waters. 
 THE TAKEAWAY 
 NOAA's Weather Prediction Center has issued a Level 3 out of 4 flash flood risk for parts of Florida.
 Localized rainfall totals could exceed 2 feet by Saturday, potentially creating additional catastrophic flooding concerns.
 Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis announced that hundreds of National Guard members and other state first responders had been mobilized Thursday.
 Unrelenting rain is expected to continue into Saturday along Florida’s Space and Treasure coasts after more than a foot of precipitation has fallen across parts of the state’s Atlantic Coast since Tuesday, triggering water rescues and evacuations and prompting Gov. Ron DeSantis to activate the National Guard on Thursday.
 Gov. DeSantis announced that over a thousand state personnel, including teams from the Florida Department of Transportation, National Guard, State Guard, and emergency management, have conducted nearly 200 rescues, deployed 9,000 feet of flood barriers and 20,000 sandbags, and mobilized heavy equipment and pumps to repair critical roadways like I-95 and clear floodwaters from impacted communities.

 NOAA's Weather Prediction Center (WPC) has dropped its rare Level 4 out of 4 High flash flood risk for the coast between Daytona Beach and Rockledge as the heaviest rain lifts northward. However, a Level 3 out of 4 Moderate threat remains in place from Palm Coast, Florida, into far southeast Georgia.
 This part of the state in particular is still reeling from  deadly, historic flooding earlier this month. Flood Alerts cover much of the Atlantic Coast through Saturday, including Miami.
 .@MyFDOT has deployed 750 team members, nearly 100 pieces of equipment, and more than 45 pumps. Crews are completing critical repairs to state roads, including I-95, to restore traffic and are placing barricades along flooded roadways to protect motorists. Hundreds of @FLHSMV, @FLStateGuard, @FLGuard and @MyFWC personnel are supporting life-saving operations, conducting nearly 200 rescues, including four pets. To protect critical infrastructure, @FLSERT has deployed nearly 9,000 feet of flood control barriers around essential facilities, including HCA Florida Lake Monroe Hospital, government offices in Palm Beach County, and an assisted living facility in Seminole County. Additional response efforts include 10 vacuum trucks actively pumping floodwaters in Hollywood, coordination between the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and water management districts to monitor canal levels, and teams conducting muck-and-gut operations in impacted communities. @FLSERT is also providing more than 20,000 sandbags to impacted counties and continues to mobilize additional pumps as requested. Our priority remains protecting Floridians and ensuring impacted communities have the support they need. I urge all residents to remain vigilant, avoid flooded roadways, and follow all guidance from local officials.
— Ron DeSantis (@GovRonDeSantis)  November 20, 2026 WHAT ARE FLOOD WATCHES, WARNINGS AND EMERGENCIES? 
 Cocoa Beach and Merrit Island have both tallied more than 14 inches of rain since Tuesday.
 Florida flash flood threat
 (FOX Weather / FOX Weather) 
 FOX 35 Orlando meteorologist and frequent FOX Weather guest Noah Bergren said parts of Volusia and Brevard counties could see between 12 and 20 inches of rain on Friday alone. According to the FOX Forecast Center, while there may be breaks between showers, repeated downpours are expected to last into Saturday.
 SUPER EL NIÑO COULD BE SHORT-LIVED AS MAJOR WEATHER PATTERN SHIFT BRINGS LA NIÑA INTO FOCUS 
 Gov. DeSantis announced Thursday that hundreds of National Guard members and other state first responders had been mobilized, along with 50 high-water vehicles, several airboats and swamp buggies.
 A NOTE: FOR FRIDAY, NOV. 20 No graphics with this post. I have a grave concern about our area. Some part of Volusia or Brevard County is likely going to get somewhere between 12" to 20" of rain just Friday. Where that happens, major to extreme flooding will occur. Life threatening flooding. Know what you would do if a Flash Flood Warning is issued from the National Weather Service. Do you have a way to evacuate? How to stay safe? If you live in a flood prone area, remain extremely vigilant. There will be slow moving, torrential "training" bands of heavy rain. ‣ Rain will come in waves all day Friday ‣ Rain will slowly move and lift northwards during the afternoon and evening ‣ Wind gusts at the coast could be 50-60 MPH in the evening and night tomorrow within the bands of rain coming in Please know this is as high and serious a risk of flash flooding I have seen in a very long time. Referring to Brevard and Volusia counties somewhere.
— Noah Bergren (@NbergWX)  November 20, 2026 The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC) also reported that about 235 emergency responders were deployed Thursday and helped rescue more than 90 residents at a flooded apartment complex in Broward County.
 In another rescue, first responders were attempting to reach an infant who had stopped breathing when their vehicle became stuck in floodwaters. An FWC officer immediately responded and was able to transport the infant to emergency personnel.
 HOLLYWOOD, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 18: Capt. Jeff Carroll, a law enforcement officer from the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission, helps Marian Lopez evacuate as floodwaters inundate the neighborhood on November 18, 2026 in Hollywood, Florida. 
 ((Photo by Joe Raedle/Getty Images) / Getty Images) 
 The Brevard County Sheriff's Office told FOX Weather Thursday that the worst flooding was concentrated around  Cocoa , Rockledge and Merritt Island .
 Video from FOX Weather Correspondent Brandy Campbell showed inundated roads and neighborhoods in Rockledge on Thursday.
 The City of Palm Bay also announced mandatory evacuations for residents of Palm Bay Estates, located west of the canal and east of the railroad tracks, due to ongoing flooding concerns.
 01:35 Crews urge nearby residents to assist with rescue of animals from flooded farm 
 FOX 35 Orlando's David Martin was live when the rescue of the farm animals was taking place. He spoke to one of the crew members who pleaded with nearby residents for assistance with the removal of animals from the flooded farm.
 Officials said communities along the nearby St. Johns River are facing some of the most dangerous conditions as water levels remain at a record high near Cocoa. Crews deployed pumps to funnel water into a nearby canal to prevent additional flooding in residential areas.
 The river is one of the slowest-draining in the county and had remained in major flood stage following the historic rain event earlier this month.
 HOLLYWOOD, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 18: Daniel Supienski and his daughter Dezirae Supienski, 9, use a kayak to paddle around the flooded streets near their home on November 18, 2026 in Hollywood, Florida. 
 ((Photo by Joe Raedle/Getty Images) / Getty Images) 
 Brevard County opened shelters in Cocoa and Melbourne Thursday for displaced residents.
 Flash flooding continues across parts of Florida as heavy rain slams the region, prompting emergency declarations, widespread road closures and high-water rescues.
 FLORIDA GOVERNOR DECLARES STATE OF EMERGENCY AS DEADLY FLOODING GRIPS SUNSHINE STATE 
 Cars driving in wet and nasty weather.
 (FOX Weather) 
 The widespread flooding first began impacting parts of South Florida Tuesday night, prompting water rescues in  Fort Lauderdale ,  Hollywood  and other parts of Broward County, as well as Miami-Dade County.
 As flooding worsened, Broward County and the cities of Fort Lauderdale and Hollywood declared states of emergency Wednesday.
 00:48 Watch: Drone video shows entire neighborhoods swamped by flash flooding in Broward County, Florida 
 Drone video shows entire neighborhoods swamped by flash flooding in Broward County, Florida, on Nov. 18, 2026.
 Potential catastrophic flooding is possible, with localized rainfall totals on Florida's Treasure Coast and Space Coast could exceed 2 feet by Saturday,
 HOW HIGH PRESSURE AND LOW PRESSURE DRIVE THE WEATHER 
 This graphic shows the expected rainfall this week for Florida.
 (FOX Weather) 
  Beyond the heavy rain and flooding, persistent onshore  winds  are expected to produce several days of rough surf and dangerous  rip currents along the state's Atlantic Coast, with wind gusts up to 60 mph possible Friday night.
 HOW TO WATCH FOX WEATHER 
 The persistent winds may also push  ocean  water toward the shoreline, potentially causing minor tidal flooding in vulnerable coastal communities, especially around high tide.
